Question:
The letter M in the figure below is first reflected over the line \(q\) and then reflected over the line \(p.\) What is the resulting image?

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Track both the letter's position and its orientation through the two reflections. A reflected point stays the same perpendicular distance from the mirror line, on the other side.

Reflecting over the diagonal line \(q\) first moves the M into the wedge to the right of the crossing, between \(q\) and \(p\), and turns it sideways. Reflecting that image over the horizontal line \(p\) then moves it below \(p\), still to the right of the vertical axis, while flipping its orientation again.

The three stages are shown here, from left to right:

[Figure 7](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q04_solution_official_reflections.png)

The final image agrees with choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). Doing one reflection at a time helps keep a correct location from being confused with a correct orientation.
